title: econ-policy-translator: convert high-level cost policies into safe serving configs + CLI simulator
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add econ-policy-translator service and rw-econctl simulator; introduces new econpolicy v1 schema and safe defaults for batch/caching/quant profiles. Non-breaking: default runtime behavior unchanged unless policy is applied.
description:
Motivation: customers want a declarative way to express cost/performance goals (target p50 latency, cost-per-1k tokens, and quality guardrails) and have those translated into safe serving runtime configs (batching, cache TTLs, quant profiles, prefill strategies) without hand-tuning. This PR introduces an econ-policy-translator service + a lightweight CLI simulator so operators can validate the effects of a policy before applying it to production.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Implements econpolicy.v1 (YAML schema), a translator that maps high-level goals to runtime knobs, safety clamps to prevent regressions, a simulation harness (rw-econctl simulate) that runs synthetic workload traces against a cost/latency model, and a reconciler that emits controlled runtime deltas (no hot changes to quant profiles unless explicitly approved). Includes unit tests, integration simulations, and docs for the Console workflow.

Key design points: 1) Declarative policy schema (econpolicy.v1) exposes target_type: [latency, cost, quality], constraints (max_cost_per_1k, target_p50_ms, min_quality_score) and strategy hints (prefer_batching, prefer_cache, quant_tolerance). 2) Translator produces candidate runtime configs: batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, cache_ttl_ms, quant_profile (none, q4_0, q5_1), prefill_strategy, and a confidence score. 3) Safety layer: automatic clamps (max_token_multiplier, no_auto_quant_for_models_with_sensitive_tags), a simulated A/B check run, and manual approval gating for quant changes. 4) CLI simulator (rw-econctl) accepts traces or sample request shape distributions and shows projected unit economics, latency percentiles, and model-quality risk. 5) Reconciler: emits policy -> delta proposals to the runtime API (not applied automatically by default; can be toggled per-team).

Checklist:
- [x] econpolicy.v1 schema and validation
- [x] translator core logic + unit tests
- [x] rw-econctl CLI with simulate/apply modes (apply is a gated operation)
- [x] simulation harness plugging into existing cost/latency model service
- [x] reconciler emits non-destructive proposals and change preview endpoints
- [x] docs and Console guide for "Policy -> Simulate -> Apply" flow
- [x] safety clamps implemented and tested

Commits summary:
- feat(econ): add econpolicy v1 schema and validation helpers
- feat(econ/translator): implement mapping rules from policy to runtime knobs
- feat(cli): add rw-econctl simulate/apply subcommands
- feat(sim): wire simulator to cost/latency model and synthetic trace runner
- feat(reconciler): proposal endpoints and preview API
- test(econ): unit + integration tests for translator and safety clamps
- docs: add policy quickstart and Console screenshots

Files changed (high-level):
- services/econ-policy-translator/    (new service; core translator + safety engine)
- cli/rw-econctl/                     (new CLI: simulate, plan, apply --apply gated)
- simulator/                          (hook into existing cost-latency model, new trace runners)
- runtime/api/v1/policy_preview.go     (preview endpoints, RBAC gated)
- infra/k8s/econ-policy-deploy.yaml    (helm overlay + canary annotation)
- docs/console/policies.md             (user guide for policy lifecycle)

Testing & CI: All unit and integration tests pass. The simulation CI job runs a suite of 14 representative traces (web-search, chat-short, code-complete) and validates unit-econ projection vs baseline +/- 10%. The e2e job exercises a non-destructive workflow.
